message.content: Both open claims are decidable by direct runtime measurement against the kernel's own `run()` over representable FP16 inputs. I'll launch two independent probes together: c1 scans the full finite FP16 domain (with per-branch breakdown), c2 focuses on the upper branch / large magnitudes and the FP16 values straddling the 2.4142 and 0.66 branch boundaries.

function.arguments:
{"claim_id": "c1", "code": "import sys, json, struct
sys.path.insert(0, "/root/cases/case_147")
import torch, numpy as np
from kernel import run

# Enumerate ALL finite FP16 bit patterns (excludes +/-Inf and NaN)
bits = np.arange(0, 65536, dtype=np.uint16)
fp16 = bits.view(np.float16)
finite = np.isfinite(fp16)
vals = fp16[finite]
n = vals.size

x = torch.from_numpy(vals.copy()).to("cuda")
out = run(x).cpu().numpy()
ref = np.atan(vals.astype(np.float64))
err = np.abs(out.astype(np.float64) - ref)

mag = np.abs(vals.astype(np.float64))
branch = np.where(mag > 2.414213562373095, "upper",
         np.where(mag > 0.66, "middle", "small"))

def stats(m):
    if not m.any(): return None
    i = np.argmax(err[m])
    return {"count": int(m.sum()), "max_abs_err": float(err[m].max()),
            "worst_input": float(vals[m][i]), "worst_out": float(out[m][i]),
            "worst_ref": float(ref[m][i])}

res = {
  "n_tested": int(n), "tolerance": 1e-6,
  "num_violations": int((err > 1e-6).sum()),
  "global_max_abs_err": float(err.max()),
  "worst_input": float(vals[np.argmax(err)]),
  "worst_out": float(out[np.argmax(err)]),
  "worst_ref": float(ref[np.argmax(err)]),
  "by_branch": {b: stats(branch == b) for b in ["small", "middle", "upper"]},
}
print(json.dumps(res))
", "expected_signal": "max absolute error vs FP64 atan over all finite FP16 values, per-branch breakdown, count of values exceeding 1e-6", "timeout_s": 300}

{"claim_id": "c2", "code": "import sys, json
sys.path.insert(0, "/root/cases/case_147")
import torch, numpy as np
from kernel import run

bits = np.arange(0, 65536, dtype=np.uint16)
vals = bits.view(np.float16)
vals = vals[np.isfinite(vals)]
mag = np.abs(vals.astype(np.float64))

# c2 focus set: upper branch (|x|>2.414, incl 65504), boundary clusters near 2.4142 and 0.66
upper = mag > 2.414213562373095
b_up = np.abs(mag - 2.414213562373095) < 0.01
b_mid = np.abs(mag - 0.66) < 0.01
focus = upper | b_up | b_mid
fvals = vals[focus]

x = torch.from_numpy(fvals.copy()).to("cuda")
out = run(x).cpu().numpy()
ref = np.atan(fvals.astype(np.float64))
err = np.abs(out.astype(np.float64) - ref)
fmag = np.abs(fvals.astype(np.float64))
grp = np.where(fmag > 2.414213562373095, "upper", np.where(np.abs(fmag-2.414213562373095) < 0.01, "near_2.414", "near_0.66"))

def stats(m):
    if not m.any(): return None
    i = np.argmax(err[m])
    return {"count": int(m.sum()), "max_abs_err": float(err[m].max()),
            "worst_input": float(fvals[m][i]), "worst_out": float(out[m][i]),
            "worst_ref": float(ref[m][i])}

res = {
  "n_focus": int(fvals.size), "tolerance": 1e-6,
  "num_violations": int((err > 1e-6).sum()),
  "max_abs_err": float(err.max()),
  "worst_input": float(fvals[np.argmax(err)]),
  "worst_out": float(out[np.argmax(err)]),
  "worst_ref": float(ref[np.argmax(err)]),
  "boundary_fp16_values_around_2.414": sorted(set(float(v) for v in fvals[b_up & (fmag <= 2.5)])),
  "boundary_fp16_values_around_0.66": sorted(set(float(v) for v in fvals[b_mid])),
  "by_group": {g: stats(grp == g) for g in ["upper", "near_2.414", "near_0.66"]},
}
print(json.dumps(res))
", "expected_signal": "max absolute error on upper branch (large |x| up to 65504) and near the 2.414/0.66 branch boundaries", "timeout_s": 300}
